meta.timeBasis: Hawaii local time 7 Dec 1941 (UTC-10:30). Tokyo time minus 19h30m.
meta.nameOrder: Western order (given name first). Japanese sources give surname first.
meta.researchLimits: Direct page fetching was blocked on this machine and the web-search quota ran out part-way through. Facts were checked against search-result summaries of the listed sources plus the author's prior knowledge of the literature. No source page was read in full. Every waypoint between documented anchors is a geometric model, flagged in 'basis'.
meta.coordinateNote: Ship and airfield target coordinates here are approximations derived from the Arizona/Missouri/Utah memorial anchors and a 045/225 Battleship Row axis. Prefer the project's dedicated ship-position dataset where it disagrees.

aborts.note: 189 planned, 6 failed to launch or aborted: 1 B5N level bomber (Kaga), 3 D3A (1 Shokaku, 2 Zuikaku), 2 A6M (1 Soryu, 1 Shokaku per navweaps; some lists put the second fighter abort on Zuikaku instead).

launch.basis: Estimated. Sources say about 230 nm due north of Oahu. Back-projected along the Opana radar track (first plot 132-136 statute miles, 3 deg east of north of Opana at 07:02) at the roughly 160 kt ground speed the radar plots imply. Aligned with kido_butai.json, which independently adopts 25.446 N 157.862 W for the 06:20 departure.
launch.note: Launch start is given as 06:00, 06:05, 06:10 or 06:18 in different accounts; 15 minutes to launch 183 aircraft is consistent across them. Departure about 06:20.

rendezvous.basis: Computed from the Japanese attack plan: 20 nautical miles bearing 340 deg from Kaena Point, altitude 1,000 m (below cloud if cloud at that height).

recovery.basis: Position and 10:10 first-landing time aligned with the sibling file kido_butai.json (recovery area about 180-190 nm north of Kahuku Point; 10:10 per Prange as recalled there). Both are low-confidence estimates.

weather.enRoute: Dense cloud layer below the formation, base about 1,500 m and tops about 2,000 m, breaking up near Oahu. Formation flew above it at 2,800-4,300 m. North-easterly tail wind.
weather.overOahu: KGMB weather heard by Fuchida: partly cloudy, mostly over the mountains, cloud base 3,500 ft (about 1,070 m), visibility good, wind north 10 kt. Cloud drifting over Battleship Row spoiled some level-bombing runs.

ordnance.levelBomb: Type 99 No. 80 Mk 5 armour-piercing bomb, about 797-800 kg, converted from a 40/41 cm naval shell. One per B5N2.
ordnance.torpedo: Type 91 Mod 2 aerial torpedo, 45 cm, about 838-848 kg, 204 kg warhead, with wooden breakaway tail fins and anti-roll stabilisers for shallow water. One per B5N2.
ordnance.diveBomb: Type 98 No. 25 land (general-purpose) bomb, about 242-250 kg. One per D3A1.
ordnance.fighter: A6M2 Model 21: two 20 mm cannon and two 7.7 mm machine guns.

crossFileNotes.note: warnings.json places the 07:02 plot at 23.5934, -157.9009 and the 07:30 plot at 22.3639, -157.9542, matching this file. Its last plot (07:39, 22 statute miles) is at 22.0019, -157.9697, about 3 nm north of where this file's track is at 07:39. The 07:40 deployment point here (21.90, -157.99) was set about 3 nm further south than the radar implies so that the documented attack times (Kaneohe 07:48, Wheeler 07:51, Ewa 07:53, Ford Island 07:55) can be met at plausible speeds. Moving it north to match the radar delays every arrival by about one minute.
Launch, departure and recovery positions follow kido_butai.json.
Soryu's fighter leader appears as Masaji Suganami here and Masaharu Suganami in kido_butai.json; both readings are in print.

In Fuchida's chutai the sighting aircraft (pilot CPO Akira Watanabe, bombardier PO1c Yanosuke Aso) moved ahead of Fuchida's own plane for the run.

route.note: Over the south-west end of Battleship Row (California). Anti-aircraft fire begins; Fuchida's plane is holed.
Over the north-east end of the row. Fuchida's lead chutai does not release: cloud covered the aim point at the drop.

attacks.description: Run from the south-west along the long axis of the row. Fuchida's own five-plane chutai aborted at the release point. What Akagi's 2nd and 3rd chutai dropped on, and when, is not established in the sources reviewed; some chutai across the four carriers made up to three runs.

Fuchida's chutai circled right over Honolulu and was starting its second run when Arizona blew up. Smoke hid the northern ships, so Fuchida shifted to Maryland, which he judged untouched, and dropped. He watched through the floor port and called two hits.

results.effect: Fuchida claimed two hits. Maryland did take two AP bomb hits that morning (one through the forecastle awning, one entering the hull forward below the waterline, flooding forward compartments). Zimm argues Fuchida's own bombs missed (two burrowed into Ford Island, the rest fell in the harbour), so the Maryland hits may belong to another chutai.
results.hitLocation: forecastle forward (through the awning), and port bow near frame 10 about 22 ft below the waterline

egress.note: Fuchida's chutai turns right after the aborted pass.
Circling over Honolulu waiting for another chance.
Offshore south of Hickam, heading west to re-enter the run.
Fuchida's own aircraft stays over Pearl Harbor to observe and to direct the second wave. The other Akagi level bombers leave for the rendezvous.
Other Akagi level bombers at the rendezvous 20 nm, 340 deg from Kaena Point.
Recovery aboard Akagi (estimated). Fuchida himself left Oahu about 10:00 and landed about 13:00, the last aircraft back.

attacks.description: Nagai passed up Utah, crossed the south end of Ford Island and attacked the ships at 1010 Dock, the usual berth of the fleet flagship. The dock runs roughly parallel to Battleship Row, so a hit on the outboard (starboard) side implies a run from the north-west across the south end of Ford Island; the bearing is an estimate.

torpedoAttack.summary: Forty B5N2s attacked in about 11 minutes (07:55 to about 08:06). About 36 torpedoes were released and 19 are counted as hits in the modern reconstruction. Two streams: Soryu and Hiryu (16) from the west against the carrier moorings on the north-west side of Ford Island, with some diverting to 1010 Dock and Battleship Row; Akagi and Kaga (24) south past Ewa, over Hickam and down Southeast Loch against Battleship Row.

sequence.note: First torpedoes of the raid. Utah 2, Raleigh 1, the rest missed. Approach from the west over Pearl City, heading about 125 deg.
Nagai. Run from the north-west across the south end of Ford Island (estimated heading 130 deg). Torpedo ran under Oglala and hit Helena.
Murata's first chutai down Southeast Loch, heading about 310 deg. First hits on both ships. Hits per aircraft not established.
Matsumura and Oku, having come round over Hickam and cut into the Akagi stream. Two hits claimed; Oku's photographed.
Kadono's element, same line as Nagai. All missed. Zimm's text implies six aircraft here and only two Hiryu aircraft on Battleship Row.
Second Akagi chutai (Lt Jinichi Goto). Some accounts send one or two of these to California.
Last unit in, a few minutes behind Akagi in a loose string, into alerted defences. Five shot down; about eight torpedoes released. One hit Nevada at about 08:03.
Mori, on his second run after breaking off from 1010 Dock. Hit claimed.

release.runDepthNote: Depth setting is given as 4 m or 6 m in different accounts; not verified this session. Harbour depth was about 12-14 m (40-45 ft).
release.note: Level release at about 160 kt from 10-20 m, the method worked out at Kagoshima for a 12 m harbour. The NPS timeline describes the planes as 'just 20 feet above' the water; Wikipedia's Type 91 article quotes 180 kt at 20 m. Range figures are estimates: Southeast Loch gives roughly 900-1,200 m of open water in front of Battleship Row.

west_virginia.note: Seven confirmed (Zimm, De Virgilio). The 1942 damage report said four or five; NHHC says as many as nine.

oklahoma.note: Capsized about 08:08. Early report: three or more. Usual modern figure five; NHHC allows up to nine.

california.note: Two hits, port side about frames 52 and 101. Well documented by the Bureau of Ships.

arizona.note: One hit claimed by a Kaga crew and reported by Vestal witnesses; not supported by the wreck.

utah.note: The six torpedoes were shared between Utah and Raleigh. Utah capsized about 08:12.

raleigh.note: Launch count is included in Utah's six.

helena.note: Nagai's hit, via under Oglala. Oglala capsized from the blast damage about 10:00.

totals.note: Battleship Row launch counts (12, 9, 3, 1) are Zimm's. The 6 and 5 for the Utah group and 1010 Dock, and so the total of 36, are this file's reconstruction. Other tallies: NHHC 'up to 21 of 29' on Battleship Row; one secondary source says 13 of 40.

illustrativeAllocationByCarrier.note: A modelling aid only. It is one allocation that satisfies Zimm's per-ship launch totals and Stille's narrative; the sources reviewed do not give a plane-by-plane assignment for Akagi and Kaga.

torpedoAttack.kagaLosses: See groups[torpedo_kaga].losses: Southeast Loch (AII-356), Naval Hospital grounds, close astern of Nevada, on land north of Fort Weaver, and one unlocated.

levelBombing.summary: Forty-nine B5N2s in ten chutai ran up Battleship Row from the south-west at 3,000 m, each chutai dropping together on its lead bombardier. Forty-nine bombs gave ten confirmed hits: two each on Arizona, Tennessee, Maryland, West Virginia and Vestal. Six of the ten were duds, broke up or detonated low-order. One of the two on Arizona destroyed the ship.
levelBombing.bombFallNote: Approximate free-fall time from 3,000 m; computed, not sourced.
levelBombing.alternativeCounts: Japanese claims and the Bureau of Ships count give Arizona four hits and three near misses. One secondary source gives eight hits from the 49 bombs.
levelBombing.repeatRuns: Cloud and smoke forced several chutai to go round again; Fuchida says some made three runs. His own chutai released on its second run.

signals.meaning: Intended as a repeat for the fighters. Two flares meant 'surprise lost': dive bombers and fighters go first to suppress the defences.
signals.note: Fuchida says he fired again because Suganami's fighters had not reacted. Takahashi took the two together as 'surprise lost' and led the dive bombers in at once; Murata, seeing this, hurried the torpedo planes. Zimm argues the interval was too short for Fuchida's version and that he meant to fire two. The 10-second gap is illustrative.
Keyed by Fuchida's radioman, PO1c Tokunobu Mizuki.
Sent to Akagi; also heard directly aboard Nagato in the Inland Sea. Sent before the first bomb fell on Pearl Harbor.

timeline.event: Six carriers about 230 nm north of Oahu begin launching the first wave (also given as 06:05-06:18).
183 of 189 aircraft airborne after about 15 minutes; six fail to launch.
Fuchida leads the formation south.
Sunrise. The formation is above a solid cloud layer with tops near 2,000 m.
Opana radar station picks up the wave 132-136 statute miles out, 3 deg east of north.
Fuchida sights the north shore of Oahu through a break in the cloud.
Opana loses the echo in ground clutter about 20 statute miles out.

Off Kahuku Point. Fuchida fires one flare, then a second; the wave deploys. Kaneohe fighters turn east, dive bombers climb and head down the centre of the island, level bombers and torpedo planes turn west along the north shore.
Eleven Zeros from Shokaku and Zuikaku begin strafing NAS Kaneohe Bay.
Fuchida orders 'To-To-To'.
Zuikaku's 25 dive bombers begin bombing Wheeler Field. The torpedo force splits into its attack groups.
'Tora-Tora-Tora'. Marines at Ewa see torpedo planes passing toward Pearl Harbor and fighters coming over the hills from Nanakuli.
Shokaku dive bombers hit Ford Island and Hickam. Soryu torpedo planes release at Utah and Raleigh. Akagi and Kaga fighters start strafing Ewa.
Torpedoes hit Utah (two) and Raleigh (one).
Murata's Akagi torpedo planes begin hitting West Virginia and Oklahoma. Nagai's torpedo hits Helena.
'AIR RAID PEARL HARBOR X THIS IS NOT DRILL'. Matsumura's Hiryu pair torpedo West Virginia.
Kaga's torpedo planes begin their runs into heavy fire; five are shot down in the next few minutes.
Level bombers begin their runs up Battleship Row from the south-west at 3,000 m. Fuchida's lead chutai aborts.
A Kaga torpedo hits Nevada forward.
Two torpedoes hit California. Kaga level bombers hit Arizona aft and Vestal.
A Hiryu level bomber's bomb detonates Arizona's forward magazines (traditional time 08:10).
Oklahoma capsizes. AP bombs hit Tennessee's turrets; fragments mortally wound West Virginia's captain.
Hirano's Akagi Zero crashes at Fort Kamehameha. Soryu and Hiryu fighters are strafing Ewa.
Utah capsizes.
Fuchida's chutai bombs Maryland on its second run.
First-wave units begin withdrawing toward the rendezvous north-west of Kaena Point. A lull follows until the second wave arrives at about 08:54.
A lone Zero strafes Bellows Field.
Bombers and fighters assembled at the rendezvous (20 nm, 340 deg from Kaena Point, 1,000 m) and heading north.
First-wave aircraft begin landing on the carriers, about 190 nm north of Oahu.
Fuchida, who stayed over Oahu through the second wave, lands on Akagi.

losses.note: Whole raid: 29 aircraft. Aircrew figure is arithmetic (5 x 3 + 1 x 2 + 3).

numberBlocks.note: Three-digit number after the prefix; first digit gives the aircraft type.

tailCodeColor.note: Codes were red, thinly outlined in white on dark-painted tails. Fuchida's aircraft was the exception.

commandStripes.rule: Horizontal stripes across the fin and rudder: three for a hikotaicho (air group leader), two for a buntaicho (division leader), one for a shotaicho (section leader).
commandStripes.colors: Usually reconstructed in the carrier division's colour: blue for Soryu and Hiryu, white for Shokaku and Zuikaku, red for Kaga. Akagi's are shown as red in some reconstructions and yellow in others.
commandStripes.note: One j-aircraft summary describes a group leader's marking as two wide bands above the code and a narrow one below. Stripe colours were not verified this session.
